objects.doc: read, write, and edit workspace files
run shell commands in the workspace
the epic/issue board — decompose work into dispatchable issues
durable memories that survive context compaction
show yourself a file, a value, or a function's documentation — the only way material enters your context
fetch a program you already ran, and hand a patched copy back to be run
return your verdict on the work you are reviewing

meta.name: List
meta.doc:
List the functions available on this API object, each with a one-line summary.

Only the functions this run actually bound are returned, so the directory never names a call your program cannot make. Open a view of one function's full signature, argument descriptions and types with `view.OpenDocsView`.

Returns: the functions this object really bound, each with its one-line summary.

session.name: Finish

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: Your last word: for the root agent the run's final text, for a subagent its return value to whoever asked for the work. It must not be empty.

session.doc:
Declare the work complete.

It sets a flag on gg's side and **returns normally**. It does not stop your program, it throws nothing, and nothing after it is refused: the flag is what gg reads once the program has ended. Calling it again simply replaces the declaration.

The flag is revoked if your program then fails — an uncaught exception, or a sandbox ceiling stopping it. A program that did not run to its end did not run the checks its summary claims, so the session carries on and you are told the ending was cancelled.

Bound only for an agent doing work; a reviewer ends with `review.Approve` instead.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` when your role does not end this way, and `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an empty summary.

session.name: Approve
session.doc:
Declare the work under review acceptable.

It takes nothing, deliberately: an approval carries no further obligation, and a shape that demanded prose would be a shape gg had to read back. It ends the session under the same rules `harness.Finish` does — it returns normally, and it is revoked if your program then fails.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` when your role is not the one that returns a verdict.

session.name: RequestChanges

parameters.name: items
parameters.doc: One entry per change, each saying what is wrong and what to change. At least one, and none of them blank.

session.doc:
Declare the work unacceptable, listing every change that must be made before it can be accepted.

Ends the session under the same rules `harness.Finish` does. A rejection with nothing to act on gives the agent that has to fix the work no work to do, which is why the empty case is refused rather than represented.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` when your role is not the one that returns a verdict, and `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an empty list or a blank entry.

views.name: OpenFile

signatures.signature: OpenFile(string path, uint? offset = null, uint? limit = null) -> FileRead

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file to read and show. Relative to your workspace, or absolute.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.doc: The 1-based first line. Leave it out to show the whole file.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.doc: How many lines. Leave it out to show to the end.

views.doc:
Read a file and show it to yourself.

The read's result comes back exactly as `fs.ReadFile` returns it, and the file is added to your context window as its own item. The separation is the point: `fs.ReadFile` gets bytes for your program, this shows a file to you, and a program that reads forty files to grep them still puts nothing in your window.

The key is the path and the region together, so two pages of one file are two views and coexist. Opening the same page again replaces it rather than piling up a duplicate.

Returns: the same read `fs.ReadFile` would have returned.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for a missing path, and `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` when a view cap this program has spent refuses it.

views.name: OpenText

parameters.name: label
parameters.doc: What to file it under. It is also what `view.Close` takes, so an empty label is refused: a view with no selector could never be closed or replaced.

parameters.name: body
parameters.doc: The text to show. Empty is allowed — it is how a program says that something it was showing is now empty.

views.doc:
Show yourself a value you computed, under a label.

This is the call that answers "how do I see the result of my own program". Opening the same label again replaces what it showed, so a label names a thing rather than a moment.

```csharp
var failed = system.Shell("cargo nextest run --workspace");
view.OpenText("tests", failed.Output);
```

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an empty label, and `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` naming the cap a body or label went over.

views.name: OpenDocsView

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The name you call the function by — `ReadFile`, `CreateIssue`, `Finish`.

views.doc:
Show yourself the full documentation for one function.

Its signature, its description, what to put in each argument, and the declarations of any types it refers to that you have not already been shown. It is a view rather than a return value: the documentation reaches you in your next prompt, under a `Documentation` heading, and can be closed like anything else.

```csharp
view.OpenDocsView("CreateIssue");
```

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for a name no function on this surface has.

views.name: Close

parameters.name: selector
parameters.doc: A file view's workspace path, or a text view's label.

views.doc:
Close every view whose selector matches, and hand back how many went.

For a file, every page of that path closes. Closing a selector that is not open returns zero; it is not a failure.

Returns: how many views were closed.

views.name: Current
views.doc:
What is open in your window right now.

It is called `Current` rather than `List` because every API object already carries a `view.List` that lists the object's own functions.

Returns: every view you hold, with what each of them costs you.

programs.name: History
programs.doc:
The programs you have run, oldest first.

Each entry carries the shape of a program rather than its source — a directory that inlined sixty lines per entry would put the whole session back into the one place that exists to avoid re-reading it. Empty before your first program has been recorded.

Returns: one summary per program you have run, oldest first.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` when this agent keeps no program library.

programs.name: Get

parameters.name: turn
parameters.doc: The turn to fetch, as `ProgramSummary.Turn` reports it. Leave it out for the most recent one.

programs.doc:
The exact source of one program, as it was run.

"As it was run" is the contract that matters: when a turn's program was itself handed over by an earlier one, what is kept is the program that executed rather than the few lines that asked for it. So fetching, patching and re-running composes.

Returns: that program's source.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` — naming the turns that are held — for a turn that ran no program, or one the library's retention has already dropped.

programs.name: Rerun

parameters.name: source
parameters.doc: The program to run instead. Blank is refused.

programs.doc:
Hand gg a program to run in place of this one.

It is **registered, not performed**. The call returns and the rest of your program still runs; only when it has ended does gg compile and run what you handed over. Everything the registering program did stands — its calls, its views — and the program that runs next sees exactly the world it left behind.

```csharp
var previous = programs.Get();
programs.Rerun(previous.Replace("--release", "--debug"));
```

The first call stands and a second is refused: a silently replaced program is a change you cannot see. The request is revoked if your program then fails, on the same rule an ending is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for a blank source, and `ToolErrorCode.Refused` for a second call in one turn.

tools.name: Shell

signatures.signature: Shell(string command, double? timeoutSeconds = null) -> ShellOutput

parameters.name: command
parameters.doc: The command line, run by `sh -c` with your workspace as its working directory.

parameters.name: timeoutSeconds
parameters.doc: How long to let it run before killing it. Leave it out for gg's default of 120 seconds. It is clamped to whatever is left of the run's wall-clock budget either way, so one call cannot outlive the run it belongs to.

tools.name: ReadFile

signatures.signature: ReadFile(string path, uint? offset = null, uint? limit = null) -> FileRead

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file to read. Relative to your workspace, or absolute for anything else in this container.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.doc: The 1-based first line to read. Leave it out to start at the beginning. Honoured only under a capped read policy; under the unlimited policy the whole file comes back.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.doc: How many lines to read. Leave it out to read to the end.

tools.doc:
Read a file, handing back a `TextFile` or an `ImageFile` — the format is detected from the file's bytes, never from its extension.

This gets bytes for your *program* and puts nothing in your context window; `view.OpenFile` is the call that shows the file to you. A relative path resolves against your workspace; an absolute one is read as given, so anything in this container — an offloaded command's output under `/tmp/gg-shell`, say — is readable.

Reading an image describes it to your program — label, media type, byte size — and does not show it to you: the pixels reach neither your program nor your context window, so a file you only read is a file you have not looked at.

Returns: the file's text window, or the picture's description.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for a missing path.

tools.name: WriteFile

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: Where to write. Relative to your workspace, or absolute. Parent directories are created for you.

parameters.name: contents
parameters.doc: The UTF-8 text to write. It replaces the file entirely.

tools.doc:
Write UTF-8 text to a file, creating parent directories and replacing any existing file.

Writing is the expensive direction of this sandbox — rewriting more than a few dozen large files in one program exhausts its fuel budget, so split a large rewrite across several turns.

Returns: how many bytes were written.

tools.name: EditFile

signatures.signature: EditFile(string path, string oldString, string newString) -> void

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file to edit.

parameters.name: oldString
parameters.doc: The exact text to find, including its whitespace. It must appear exactly once.

parameters.name: newString
parameters.doc: The text to put in its place. An empty string deletes the match.

tools.doc:
Replace the one exact occurrence of some text in a file with something else.

Widen the surrounding context until the match is unique rather than counting occurrences.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` when the text does not appear, and `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` — with the number of matches — when it appears more than once.

tools.name: ListDir

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The directory to list, relative to your workspace or absolute. Leave it out to list your workspace root.

tools.doc:
List a directory, sorted by name.

Each entry carries a bare `DirEntry.Name` — join it with the directory you listed — and its `DirEntry.Kind`. An empty directory is an empty list, not a failure.

Returns: the directory's entries, sorted by name.

tools.name: ReadSkill

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The skill's name, exactly as your system prompt lists it. An unknown one comes back with the full list of the ones you have.

tools.doc:
Read an authored skill by name and hand back its body, front matter stripped.

Reading a skill also pins it permanently into your session's context, so it survives a compaction and you never have to read it twice. A skill that carries code binds that code at `lib.<name>` for every later program of yours.

Returns: the skill's body.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for a name this run has no skill under.

tools.name: WriteMemory

signatures.signature: WriteMemory(string name, string description, string body, string? code = null, string? onUse = null) -> MemoryUsage

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The unique short name this memory is addressed by.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: A one line description of what it holds.

parameters.name: body
parameters.doc: The memory itself.

parameters.name: code
parameters.doc: Reusable C# bound at `lib.<name>` in every later program of yours. It is not context: it costs you no window, is never shown back to you, and counts against no body limit.

parameters.name: onUse
parameters.doc: A program to run once, the moment this memory first comes into use. It runs after the program that loaded the memory has ended, so whatever views it opens reach you on your next turn.

tools.doc:
Record a new durable memory.

A duplicate name, or a body that would breach a limit, is a failure — revise or evict rather than accruing more.

Returns: how full your memory budget now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` for a name you already hold, and `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` for a body that would breach a cap.

tools.name: UpdateMemory

signatures.signature: UpdateMemory(string name, string description, string body, string? code = null, string? onUse = null) -> MemoryUsage

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The memory to replace, by the name you gave it.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: Its new one line description.

parameters.name: body
parameters.doc: Its new body, in full.

parameters.name: code
parameters.doc: Reusable C# bound at `lib.<name>`, replacing whatever it carried before.

parameters.name: onUse
parameters.doc: A program to run once, when this memory next comes into use.

tools.doc:
Replace an existing memory's description and body.

The whole memory is replaced, so hand back everything it should still say. `memory.EditMemory` is the call that changes part of one.

Returns: how full your memory budget now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for a memory you do not hold.

tools.name: CreateMemory

signatures.signature: CreateMemory(string name, string description, string body, string? code = null, string? onUse = null) -> MemoryUsage

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The unique short name this memory is addressed by.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: A one line description — this is the part that stays in your window.

parameters.name: body
parameters.doc: The memory itself, which does not.

parameters.name: code
parameters.doc: Reusable C# bound at `lib.<name>` in every later program of yours.

parameters.name: onUse
parameters.doc: A program to run once, on the read that first loads this memory.

tools.doc:
Record a new memory file, whose contents stay out of your context window until read.

The file-shaped strategies' way of writing one: what is pinned is the index line, and the body costs you nothing until `memory.ReadMemory` fetches it.

Returns: how full your memory budget now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` for a name you already hold.

tools.name: ReadMemory

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The memory's slug, as your index lists it.

tools.doc:
Read one memory's contents back, by name.

Returns: the memory's body.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for a memory you do not hold.

tools.name: EditMemory

signatures.signature: EditMemory(string name, string search, string replace) -> MemoryUsage

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The memory to revise.

parameters.name: search
parameters.doc: The exact text to replace. It must occur exactly once.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.doc: What to put in its place; empty cuts the text out.

tools.doc:
Revise a memory in place, replacing the one exact occurrence of some text.

Returns: how full your memory budget now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` when the text is not there, `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` when it is there more than once, and `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an edit that would leave the memory empty.

tools.name: SearchMemories

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.doc: The words to look for. At least one — an empty search is a failure rather than every memory.

tools.doc:
Find the memories mentioning any of these keywords, best first.

Ranked by how many distinct keywords each memory matched, then by how often they occur in it. A search that matches nothing is an empty list rather than a failure.

Returns: the memories that matched, best first, each with an excerpt around its first match.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an empty keyword list.

tools.name: DeleteMemory

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The memory to drop.

tools.doc:
Evict a memory by name, freeing room for new ones.

Returns: how full your memory budget now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for a memory you do not hold.

tools.name: AddTask

signatures.signature: AddTask(string id, string title, string? description = null, string[]? blockedBy = null) -> TaskUsage

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The unique short id other tasks reference it by.

parameters.name: title
parameters.doc: What the task is.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: A longer description, if a title does not carry it.

parameters.name: blockedBy
parameters.doc: Ids of tasks that must finish first. An edge that would create a cycle is refused.

tools.doc:
Add a task to your list.

Returns: how full your task budget now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` for an id you already used or an edge that would make a cycle, and `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` at the task cap.

tools.name: UpdateTask

signatures.signature: UpdateTask(string id, string? title = null, TextEdit description = default, TaskStatus? status = null) -> void

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The task to revise.

parameters.name: title
parameters.doc: A new title.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: A three-way edit of the description: keep it, clear it, or set it.

parameters.name: status
parameters.doc: A new status.

tools.doc:
Revise a task's title, description and status.

Everything is optional and what you leave out is left alone. The description is a `TextEdit` rather than a nullable string, so that clearing it and leaving it are different requests.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an unknown id, and `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` when you changed nothing at all.

tools.name: SetBlockedBy

signatures.signature: SetBlockedBy(string id, params string[] blockedBy) -> void

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The task whose blockers change.

parameters.name: blockedBy
parameters.doc: The ids that must finish first, replacing whatever was there. An empty list clears every blocker.

tools.doc:
Replace a task's whole blocker set.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` for an edge that would make a cycle.

tools.name: CompleteTask

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The task that is finished.

tools.doc:
Mark a task done.

Tasks it blocked become actionable once every one of their blockers is done.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an unknown id.

tools.name: RemoveTask

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The task to drop.

tools.doc:
Remove a task, and every blocker edge pointing at it.

Returns: how full your task budget now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an unknown id.

tools.name: CreateEpic

signatures.signature: CreateEpic(string prefix, string title, string description) -> EpicCreated

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.doc: A three to six letter prefix naming the epic. Upper-cased it becomes the epic's id, and the stem its issues are numbered from — `auth` gives `AUTH`, then `AUTH-1`, `AUTH-2`.

parameters.name: title
parameters.doc: What the epic is called.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: What the epic covers.

tools.doc:
Create an epic to group related issues under.

Returns: the id the prefix resolved to, and how full the board now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` for a prefix already in use, and `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` at the epic cap.

tools.name: CreateIssue

signatures.signature: CreateIssue(string title, string inScope, string outOfScope, string completionCriteria, string agent, string? description = null, string[]? blockedBy = null, string? epicId = null, string[]? reviewers = null) -> IssueCreated

parameters.name: title
parameters.doc: What the issue is called.

parameters.name: inScope
parameters.doc: What this issue is responsible for.

parameters.name: outOfScope
parameters.doc: What it is explicitly not responsible for.

parameters.name: completionCriteria
parameters.doc: How it will be judged done.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent gg dispatches this issue to. It must be one you may spawn — your system prompt lists them.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: An overview, where the title does not carry it.

parameters.name: blockedBy
parameters.doc: Ids of issues that must finish first; a cycle is refused.

parameters.name: epicId
parameters.doc: The epic to group it under.

parameters.name: reviewers
parameters.doc: The agents that must approve this issue's work, drawn from the same set as `agent`. Required when this run's reviewers feature is on, and left out otherwise.

tools.doc:
Create a self-contained, dispatchable issue, and get back the id the board assigned it.

The three scope arguments are what makes an issue dispatchable: the agent that picks it up sees them and nothing of your conversation, so anything it needs has to be in them.

```csharp
var created = project.CreateIssue(
    title: "port the fixtures to the new schema",
    inScope: "everything under tests/fixtures",
    outOfScope: "the schema itself, which is already agreed",
    completionCriteria: "cargo nextest run --workspace passes",
    agent: "worker",
    epicId: "AUTH");
```

Returns: the id the board assigned, and how full the board now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an agent you may not spawn, `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` for a blocker cycle, and `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` at the issue cap.

tools.name: UpdateIssue

signatures.signature: UpdateIssue(string id, string? title = null, TextEdit description = default, string? inScope = null, string? outOfScope = null, string? completionCriteria = null, IssueStatus? status = null, EpicAssignment epic = default) -> void

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The issue to revise.

parameters.name: title
parameters.doc: A new title.

parameters.name: description
parameters.doc: A three-way edit of the description: keep it, clear it, or set it.

parameters.name: inScope
parameters.doc: New scope.

parameters.name: outOfScope
parameters.doc: New out-of-scope.

parameters.name: completionCriteria
parameters.doc: New completion criteria.

parameters.name: status
parameters.doc: A new status.

parameters.name: epic
parameters.doc: A change of epic grouping: keep it, ungroup it, or group it under an epic.

tools.doc:
Revise an issue.

Everything is optional and what you leave out is left alone. The description and the epic grouping are three-way values rather than nullable ones, so that clearing and leaving are different requests.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an unknown id, and `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` when you changed nothing at all.

tools.name: SetIssueBlockedBy

signatures.signature: SetIssueBlockedBy(string id, params string[] blockedBy) -> void

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The issue whose blockers change.

parameters.name: blockedBy
parameters.doc: The issue ids that must finish first, replacing whatever was there. An empty list clears every blocker.

tools.doc:
Replace an issue's whole blocker set.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` for an edge that would make a cycle.

tools.name: RemoveEpic

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The epic to drop, by its id.

tools.doc:
Remove an epic. Its issues are kept, and ungrouped.

Returns: how full the board now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an unknown id.

tools.name: RemoveIssue

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The issue to drop, by its id.

tools.doc:
Remove an issue, and every blocker edge pointing at it.

Returns: how full the board now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an unknown id.

tools.name: WaitForIssue

parameters.name: id
parameters.doc: The issue to wait on.

tools.doc:
Register a wait on an issue, and get back an acknowledgement.

It does **not** block inside your program: it records the wait and returns at once, so the rest of your program still runs. Once the program has ended the run suspends — freeing this agent's slot for others — until the issue is terminal, and then resumes and tells you which way it went.

You cannot wait on the issue you were assigned to implement.

Returns: an acknowledgement that the wait is registered.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Refused` for the issue you were assigned, and `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an unknown id.

tools.name: EvictFileView

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The workspace path whose views to drop. Leave it out to drop every file view you hold.

tools.doc:
Drop file contents you have read out of your context window.

The files on disk are untouched; only your view of them goes.

Returns: what was actually freed, and from where.

tools.name: ArchiveThread

parameters.name: ranges
parameters.doc: The spans of turns to archive. Each is inclusive at both ends, and a span whose ends are equal archives one turn.

tools.doc:
Move whole turns out of your window, named by the turn numbers on your results.

Ranges are inclusive and may overlap. Your own messages in an archived turn are dropped; the results are kept and stay searchable with `context.SearchArchive`.

Returns: what was actually freed.

tools.name: SearchArchive

parameters.name: query
parameters.doc: The substring to look for.

tools.doc:
Search everything you have archived, case-insensitively, by substring.

At most eight hits, most recent first. A search that matched nothing is an empty `ArchiveSearch.Hits`; a search with nothing to look in says so through `ArchiveSearch.ArchiveEmpty`, which is a different fact.

Returns: whether there was an archive at all, and what matched.

tools.name: Compact

signatures.signature: Compact(string summary, params string[] files) -> void

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: Everything the next window has to start from: what you are doing, what you have found, and what is left.

parameters.name: files
parameters.doc: Workspace paths to read freshly into the new window.

tools.doc:
Compact your context window: gg drops the detailed thread and restarts it from your summary.

It is **registered, not performed**: the call validates and returns, your program carries on, and gg rewrites the window once the program has ended — a context reset has no shape inside the program whose context it resets. Calling it again simply replaces the request.

Skills, memories and your task list are kept regardless. gg asks for this call when the window is full and refuses every other call until it is made, so it is available at all times.

tools.name: SpawnSubagent

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent to run the child as — one of the agents you may spawn, which your system prompt lists. It selects the child's model, tools and instructions.

parameters.name: task
parameters.doc: What the child should do: `Brief.Prompt(...)` for instructions you write here, or `Brief.Issue(...)` for a board issue whose scope becomes the brief.

tools.doc:
Delegate scoped work to a child agent, and get its handle back immediately.

The child runs in parallel; nothing here waits for it. Collect it later with `agents.WaitForSubagents`.

```csharp
var child = agents.SpawnSubagent("worker", Brief.Issue("AUTH-1"));
var results = agents.WaitForSubagents(child.Id);
```

Returns: the child's handle — its id, the profile it runs as, and the model bound to it.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an agent you may not spawn, and `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` at the delegation depth cap.

tools.name: WaitForSubagents

parameters.name: ids
parameters.doc: The child ids to wait for, as `agents.SpawnSubagent` handed them back.

tools.doc:
Wait for every outstanding child, and collect their results.

This blocks while it waits, and the run's wall-clock budget keeps running while it does.

Returns: one result per child, in the order they were collected.

tools.name: SendMessage

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.doc: The child to write to.

parameters.name: message
parameters.doc: What to tell it.

tools.doc:
Deliver a message to a running child's inbox; it receives it at its next turn.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an unknown child, and `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` for one that has already returned.

tools.name: TransitionState

signatures.signature: TransitionState(string state, string? note = null) -> void

parameters.name: state
parameters.doc: The state to move to, named the way you name an agent to spawn.

parameters.name: note
parameters.doc: The opening message the next state's agent sees.

tools.doc:
Move the process you are running inside on to another of its states.

It is **registered, not performed**: the call validates the target against the states you may move to, returns, and your program carries on to its end; the transition happens after that. Replacing the agent — and its window — while its own program is still running would pull every remaining call out from under it.

The first declaration stands and a second is refused: a silently replaced successor is a change you cannot see. Bound only when a state machine is driving you and the state you are in has somewhere to go.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` names a state you may not move to, `ToolErrorCode.Refused` means you already declared a succession this turn, and `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` means no machine is driving you.

tools.name: Exec

signatures.signature: Exec(string agent, string? prompt = null) -> void

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent to become. It must be one you may become.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.doc: The opening message it sees.

tools.doc:
Continue this session as a different agent.

It takes over from your next turn with its own model, tools and instructions, keeping every capability the two of you both have — your whole conversation above all. Registered exactly as `agents.TransitionState` is, and for the same reason.

The first declaration of a succession stands, so an `Exec` after a `agents.TransitionState`, or a second `Exec`, is refused.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` names an agent you may not become, and `ToolErrorCode.Refused` means you already declared a succession this turn.

tools.name: Fork

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.doc: What this copy is to do differently from you.

tools.doc:
Run a copy of yourself, in parallel, on something you will not do yourself.

The copy has your model, your tools and a private copy of your whole conversation, so the prompt is the *difference* rather than a briefing.

Its handle comes back immediately, but the copy itself starts once this turn's results are recorded — the conversation it inherits has to be a complete one — so `agents.WaitForSubagents` can only collect it on a later turn.

Returns: the copy's handle.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` at the delegation depth cap, and `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` with no delegation runtime to collect the copy with.

helpers.name: ReadTextFile

signatures.signature: ReadTextFile(string path, uint? offset = null, uint? limit = null) -> string

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file to read. Relative to your workspace, or absolute.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.doc: The 1-based first line to read. Leave it out to start at the beginning.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.doc: How many lines to read. Leave it out to read to the end.

helpers.doc:
Read a text file and hand back its contents directly — `fs.ReadFile` without the narrowing, for the common case.

The same read, the same window, the same cost. Reading is the cheap direction of this sandbox, so a program that reads a dozen files to decide what to change is doing the right thing.

Returns: the file's text.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` when the path names a picture — use `fs.ReadFile` to inspect one, and `view.OpenFile` to look at it.

types.name: ToolErrorCode
types.declaration: enum ToolErrorCode { InvalidArgument, NotFound, Conflict, Refused, Unavailable, LimitExceeded, IOError, Other }
types.doc:
Why a gg call failed, in the vocabulary a `catch` branches on.

It is never derived from the wording of a message: every gg tool classifies its own failures where it raises them, and this is that classification. Branch on it rather than on `System.Exception.Message`, which is written for you to read and not for you to parse.

members.name: InvalidArgument
members.doc: The arguments were malformed, ill-typed, or out of range.

members.name: NotFound
members.doc: The named file, skill, memory, task, epic, issue, subagent, stored program or documentation entry does not exist.

members.name: Conflict
members.doc: Well-formed, but in conflict with how things stand: an ambiguous edit, a dependency cycle, a duplicate id, a subagent that already returned.

members.name: Refused
members.doc: gg refused the call — a rule about your own state. A memory you hold read-only, a call a pending compaction does not admit, a second succession in a turn that already declared one, or a hook that blocked it. A ceiling you ran into is `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` instead.

members.name: Unavailable
members.doc: The call exists and this run does not offer it to you: a tool outside this run's capability set, an ending your role does not declare, or a program library this agent does not keep. The recovery is to stop asking for it.

members.name: LimitExceeded
members.doc: A gg-side ceiling was hit: a shell timeout, a memory, task or board cap, the delegation depth cap, one of the view caps a program spends, or the run's wall-clock budget running out mid-program.

members.name: IOError
members.doc: The underlying I/O or process failed.

members.name: Other
members.doc: The failure was not classified. Reserved for outcomes raised outside a tool implementation; no tool produces it.

types.name: ToolException
types.declaration: sealed class ToolException : Exception

members.name: Code
members.doc: The failure class, so a catch site branches on a value rather than on prose.

members.name: Tool
members.doc: The gg tool that failed (`read_file`, `spawn_subagent`), so a catch site can report it without reading the message.
